newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa meets resistance, ends mixed.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa meets resistance, ends mixed.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures ended mixed with the active nearby months easier after failing to break through resistance, traders said.
May was most active, with 2,762 lots done. It last traded one sterling lower at 894 stg. March, with 1,885 lots done last traded one stg lower at 914.
March reached a high of 903 stg before falling back. "It's a little bit dissappointing. People were talking it up," one trader said.
There had been a lack of follow through buying he said. "Most people expect origin selling at 900 to 905," he said. Buyers were, therefore, wary of pushing prices up too high.
"They want it higher," he said. "But they're waiting for the funds to come in and do it."
He expected to see sideways trading, "until we have some decent physical news."
The International Cocoa Organisation (ICCO) completed at 4,250 tonne monthly buffer stock sale earlier in the day.
The European Commission said on Tuesday it was vetting the proposed acquisition of the cocoa business of W.R. Grace & Company by Archer Daniels Midland Co, both based in the United States.
